question: Hospital units with the best teamwork recorded more drug errors than other units. What did the researcher conclude?
options: They were more willing to report them
answer: They were more willing to report them. Edmondson expected well-led teams to make fewer errors, and was puzzled when their records showed more. Interviews showed that in those units nurses felt safe admitting mistakes; elsewhere errors stayed hidden. The best teams looked worst on paper because they could see their errors.
move: Read an error count as a measure of honesty before competence.
ask: Where I work or live, is it safe to admit a mistake, or do mistakes simply go unrecorded?
trap: More errors recorded must mean more errors made.
reference: Edmondson, Learning from mistakes is easier said than done: Group and organizational influences on the detection and correction of human error, Journal of Applied Behavioral Science, 1996
